prompt: Convert a hex string into byte values and back again by hand, two hex digits per byte. Integer.parseInt with a radix and Integer.toHexString are off limits.
explanation: Hex is base 16, so a pair of digits is a single byte: the first digit is worth 16 times the second, which is why high * 16 + low rebuilds the value. Going the other way, value / 16 is the high nibble and value % 16 the low one, and emitting both unconditionally is what keeps small values zero-padded to two characters. Using indexOf against a digit table both decodes a character and validates it, since a non-hex character returns -1.
hints: An odd-length string can never be a whole number of bytes -- reject it before the loop.
DIGITS.indexOf(c) returns the digit's value, or -1 when c is not a hex digit. Lowercase the character first so 'F' works too.
For bytesToHex, append DIGITS.charAt(value / 16) then DIGITS.charAt(value % 16) so every value produces exactly two characters.
